Arguments between rivals can escalate into an actual fight: turn-based, and stopped short (both back off once either drops to half health) - rival brawls never kill (famine cannibalism is a separate matter, see below). Off by default; turn it on if you want the drama. A block mark bans brawling for a pair outright, and setting Drama intensity to Quiet disables it even when this is on.

When a duplicant's stress maxes out and they actually break down (ugly crying / screaming / vomiting / binge eating / smashing things / throwing sparks), everyone in the room stops to watch, and the relationship keeps a memory of it. For the next few cycles, the first person to talk to them, tend to them or share their table pulls them out of it - a large affinity gain for both, and a little stress for the one who went. You can also pick that person yourself with a matchmaking mark. It changes no numbers: breakdown frequency, stress and death rate are all untouched. On by default.

After something bad happens to the colony (a death, several breakdowns, an empty larder), everyone pins it on whoever is least liked, guilty or not: a one-off affinity drop, then a slide into being frozen out - the three who like them least stop warming up at all, others flash disgust in passing, and tablemates leave early. Both exits are your tools: in act one, pair them with a well-respected colleague and that person will speak up; in act two, anyone tending, venting or eating with them breaks it. Nothing gets stuck forever - time fades it. Needs the master switch too, and Drama intensity set to Quiet disables it outright.

Master switch, off by default. The dark events below only take effect once this is on - brawls, famine cannibalism, and the tests of character added later. When the larder is empty and several duplicants are starving, the colony turns on itself and the dead become food. A warning and a countdown come first, and restocking during that window calls it off; one death per episode, and it stops once food recovers. This is the darkest content in the mod - it needs the master switch as well.

Within one trade, a duplicant who keeps getting sent somewhere dangerous (thin air, unbreathable gas, actively suffocating or burning or freezing) starts to resent the colleague who never goes down: affinity toward them can only fall, and it can end in outright rivalry. Working in an atmo suit does not count - which quietly turns "who has a suit" into a social question. The way out is yours: change the priorities. Old duty slides out of the rolling window, the grievance fades on its own, and it leaves behind "they've been going down too lately". This is the only feature in the mod resolved by you changing how you manage the colony, and it uses the game's own controls - no new UI. Two duplicants down there together counts as well: that becomes comradeship. And the same sacrifice reads differently between friends - "they went down in my place" raises affinity instead. It adds no stress and takes nothing away: the game already charges for bad environments. At most two grievances run at once. On by default; the Quiet drama preset force-disables it.

Rivals drag each other down at work

Two duplicants who have become rivals both lose work efficiency while doing the same kind of job within three tiles of each other - the mirror of the "Side by Side" bonus. It draws no blood, adds no stress, takes no morale and changes no affinity: the only thing it costs is your throughput. This is the first feature in the mod where a relationship going bad actually charges you for it. Friction only shows up during actual work: sleeping, group activities, eating and idling are untouched. Safety line: efficiency has a floor and can never reach zero however it is configured, and doctoring, healing, taking medicine, catching a breath underwater, grabbing oxygen and fleeing to safety are never slowed. The way out is yours: move one of them, or matchmake to thaw the rivalry. On by default; the Quiet drama preset force-disables it.
